prompt:
Create ONE production sprite atlas for the mobile pixel-art puzzle game matchBlade. This is a new coherent replacement tile set using the attached old tiles only as references for identity and color coding. Use case: stylized-concept / game UI sprites. Output a SQUARE PNG with genuine transparent background and EXACTLY a 3 by 3 evenly spaced grid of equal square cells. Each cell contains one complete square tile, centered, aligned at exactly the same size, occupying 92% of its cell. No labels, letters, numerals, title, watermark, scenery or extra elements. Leave transparent gutters between tiles.

Cell order, left to right, top to bottom:
ROW 1: (1) two bold crossed silver swords, crimson red inset; (2) a large PURPLE FIREBALL with a rounded blazing core and flame tail bending upward, bright pale lavender/cream core and violet flame, deep plum inset, absolutely no staff or wand; (3) a bold steel-and-blue heater shield, royal blue inset.
ROW 2: (4) one chunky gold key with a simple round bow and two teeth, rich forest green inset; (5) one large cyan faceted diamond, muted ochre inset; (6) three chunky cut wooden logs bound with one strap, warm burnt orange/brown inset.
ROW 3: (7) a bold pile of three pale slate rocks with broad facets, deep blue-gray inset; (8) a short round glass potion flask containing bright mint-green liquid, cream glass highlight and cork stopper, dark teal inset; (9) an empty charcoal inset tile frame with no symbol, for future UI use.

Art direction: charming confident handcrafted pixel art, designed to read at only 44px on a phone. Crisp blocky pixel clusters like a 42x42 logical sprite enlarged cleanly, limited cohesive palette, NO tiny speckled textures, no elaborate filigree, no gems on frames, no runes, no starbursts. ALL tiles share one understated THIN dark gunmetal frame, about 3% of tile width, small chamfered corners, one subdued highlight along the top and left edge, short dark bottom shadow. Frame should recede compared with the icon. Larger simple foreground symbols occupying 72-78% of tile face, stout contours, clear silhouettes, a few broad highlight/shadow planes only. Subdued dark backgrounds behind vivid icons. Keep swords red, magic purple, shield blue, key green, diamond cyan/gold, logs orange-brown, rocks slate. No glossy 3D rendering, no soft gradients or bloom. The fireball must look unmistakably like a ball of magical flame, not a feather, flower or wand. The atlas must have precise equal 3x3 cell spacing and no tile clipping.
refinement: Edit the attached 3-by-3 game tile atlas. Preserve the exact 3x3 cell grid, tile order, eight symbol identities, color coding, transparent background and pixel-art style. The important correction: all NINE outer steel frames are still FAR TOO THICK AND BRIGHT. Replace the large segmented metal frame on every tile with a VERY THIN, DARK, mostly flat gunmetal rim, only 3% of tile width, one small muted gray highlight on the top-left and a short dark bottom edge. Remove the big bright corner blocks, segments, bolts and gaps. The frame should look unobtrusive on a phone. Expand each colored inset and its foreground symbol into the freed space, so every symbol looks larger and takes about 78% of total tile width. Keep the roughly chamfered square outer silhouettes and exact centered positioning in the same cells. Keep the simple thick silhouettes of the sword pair, purple fireball, shield, gold key, cyan gem, logs, slate rock pile, green potion; empty ninth tile remains empty. Each foreground symbol remains fully inside its own tile and never clips the border. Quieter dark backgrounds, no decorative scratches, no extra texture, no glow around the tiles. Crisp, limited-palette pixel clusters. Do not change or add anything else. The new frame must visually recede, especially when all nine tiles are viewed together.
